messages:
cheng: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection hint change landed in canary (patch r4567) we started seeing a small but persistent bump in soft-429s on the n1 GPU pools. Putting raw observations here for context.

cheng: 1) 95p latency for batch assembly up ~18% on longer sequences (>=1024). 2) token_budget_exhausted soft-429s rose from 0.03% -> 0.7% across the canary. 3) KV hit-rate dips ~4% on tail requests when the new kernel is chosen.

maya: url: https://perf.internal.redwood/dashboard?view=canary-kernel-r4567 :eyes:

alex: Is the kernel switch making prefetch/pipeline ordering worse for mixed-sequence workloads? Could be increasing per-batch scheduling jitter so token budget gets consumed before batches form.

cheng: Yeah that's my read. Kernel selection now prefers a large-window kernel for mid-length sequences which increases per-request assembly time in mixed workloads. That pushes our continuous-batcher to keep more requests in-flight -> token burn spikes. Also the large-window kernel doesn't use the same KV prefetch path, so effective local KV hits drop.

dave: Can we avoid a full revert by tuning admission instead of kernels? Idea: adaptive token window that scales token_budget_target per-slot based on observed batch-assembly latency and kv-hit delta. If kv-hit drops, shrink token window proactively.

sara: I prototyped a tiny controller yesterday. Config example:
```
admit_controller:
  mode: adaptive
  base_token_target: 1200
  scale_rules:
    - trigger: assembled_95p_ms > 60
      factor: 0.8
    - trigger: kv_hit_delta < -0.02
      factor: 0.7
  floor: 400
  ceiling: 3600
  smoothing_ms: 30000
```

maya: Nice. How do we avoid thrashing? smoothing_ms helps, but need hysteresis on kernel choice too (kernel stickiness).

alex: Also want to ensure tail latency SLAs don't regress. Suggest we use two signals: assembled_95p and soft_429_rate. If soft_429_rate rises after adjustment -> auto rollback.

cheng: Agreed. Proposed experiment: canary rollout with 1% traffic for 30m, then 5% for 1h, then 20% for 2h. Abort criteria: soft_429_rate > 0.5% OR end-to-end p99 latency +5% sustained for 10m. Metrics to log: admit_token_target, assembled_95p_ms, kv_hit_rate, soft_429_rate, kernel_hint_id.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary/admit-adaptive-controller r789 deployed to n1-canary (1%).

sara: I'll add kernel_hint_id to the trace span and log it to perf-ingest so we can correlate which kernel was active for each assembled window.

maya: Also add a lightweight histogram of batch assembly durations per kernel_hint_id. That should show if a particular kernel is the offender.

dave: For the algorithm: compute token_target_new = clamp(base * (T_target / assembled_95p_ms), floor, ceiling) where T_target is historical baseline 95p. Multiply by kv_penalty if kv_hit_delta < 0 (kv_penalty = 0.85 per 2% drop). Use exponential smoothing. Keep the math simple and deterministic.

alex: One more thing — ensure admission controller emits a small sample of rejected payloads (anonymized sizes) so we can debug whether we accidentally shifted to rejecting many short requests.

cheng: Action items:
- sara: add kernel_hint_id trace + sample rejected payloads (30m)
- maya: add assembly-by-kernel hist and hook metrics to dashboard
- dave: implement adaptive token window algorithm and config knobs, unit tests for clamp + smoothing
- alex: add abort criteria to rollout plan and test alerting rule
- cheng: run the canary and watch soft_429_rate for first 1h, be ready to cut if needed

sara: ack, will push trace changes in PR 4569 and enable sampling at 5% for canary lanes.

maya: #follow-up: if we see kernel stickiness being the problem we can add a quick heuristic to prefer the previous kernel for 60s for a given serving slot (avoid flip-flop).

cheng: Thanks everyone. If canary looks good after the 5% stage we'll promote and schedule a kernel-policy followup to avoid future regressions. :thumbsup:

alex: LGTM, keep notes in the perf runbook so infra oncall can rollback quickly.

deploy-bot: monitor: canary/admit-adaptive-controller r789 health checks green.
